_: The one run the landing page prints in full.
`input` is the request the page describes in words; `verified` is what the
engine returned for it. Neither half is edited by hand: run
`node scripts/verify-worked-example.mjs --write` and take what the engine says.
`pnpm check` runs the same script without --write and fails if the page has
drifted, which it silently had — see the header of that script.

Of the 204 m² reserved for plant and circulation, 169 m² is drawn on the island in 2 piece(s) and 35 m² has no room on it at all. The deduction is still charged in full against the bay count.

Bays stand against all four walls and one 6 m ring aisle serves them: 26 to each long wall and 2 to each short one, less the 0 the way in and the core take. The island the ring encloses is 42.00 × 6.50 m.

Laid out as bays to the walls, the ring aisle sloped as the ramp: 56 bays, against 0 modules along the width (a straight ramp climbing a 3.2 m storey needs 6.30 × 30.27 m (DBC Tables B.9 and B.10) and this packing has 65.00 × 26.36 m); 18 modules along the depth; 0 bays to the walls, one ring aisle (a straight ramp climbing a 3.2 m storey needs 6.30 × 30.27 m (DBC Tables B.9 and B.10), reached from the ring at one end of the island, and the 42.00 × 6.50 m island does not have it clear of the core), on the same level. All 4 were packed.

The 288 m² deducted for cores, plant and the ramp landing costs about 13 bays at 21.25 m² each — the area one more bay takes inside a module, not the gross area per bay. Of it, 83 m² is the core, standing where it is drawn (0 bay(s) were not placed there), and 204 m² is the strip reserved at the edge.

Headroom (Table B.9, 2.4 m clear above any point of a ramp): the ramps stand in one strip on every level, so over each is the next, one 3.20 m storey up. The slab, its beams and anything hung below them over the ramp may be at most 0.80 m deep. No structure is drawn: this is the budget a design must fit in, not a statement that one does.

parkingInFar.verdict: The parking-in-FAR treatment moves regulatory capacity by 5355 m², but not the governing capacity: the parking limit binds below both treatments. On this plot the open regulatory question does not change the answer — though it would on a plot where the FAR ceiling binds.

workbookSheets.name: Capacity
workbookSheets.note: Three bands, never merged and never averaged. There is no "realistic" or "expected" figure in this file because the engine does not produce one — the honest substitute is the user realism discount, which defaults to 1.00.

workbookSheets.name: Parking demand
workbookSheets.note: Demand at the probe target. Compare against the "Parking level" sheet: a level that packs fewer bays than this sheet requires is a real and reportable state, not an error in either number.

workbookSheets.name: GFA calculation
workbookSheets.note: Allowed is FAR × plot area, before the parking-in-FAR treatment. Proposed is whole floors of the tower plate, plus parking only where it counts toward FAR. The residential and commercial allowances are capped separately and summed at the end. Statements with no figure — an allowance nobody stated, a floor named and not counted — are below the table, not in the value column.

workbookSheets.name: Parking level
workbookSheets.note: Bays placed as rectangles to Dubai Building Code Table B.11, not an area divided by a factor. A bay count that cannot be laid out is not a bay count.

workbookSheets.name: Assumption register
workbookSheets.note: Every gap the engine filled, why it filled it that way, and what the answer does if the assumption is wrong. Ranked by effect.

Generated capacity study, not a submission drawing.
notModelled: Columns, and therefore no grid bubbles. The layout charges Table B.11's 300 mm clearance per bay but places no column, so drawing one would be drawing structure nobody checked against the bays - and a grid bubble is read as a column line. Position on a parking sheet is given by bay number and by the dimensioned module.
Stairs and lifts as rooms, and plant. The run declares how much of each parking level they take — drawn as the reserved zone — not where each one goes.
Slab thickness. Levels are planes at their floor level. The engine computes no slab depth, and a drawn thickness would be an invented one.
Façades, windows, balconies and units. The engine computes none of them.

Neighbouring buildings and the road. The run knows which edges of the plot face a road and which face a neighbour — the site plan writes that on the boundary — but not what stands beyond them, so neither is drawn.
Pedestrian entrance, refuse room and escape distances — NOT ASSESSED until their rules are encoded.

The sloped ring is drawn level in 3D and in section. On plan the ring aisle and the bays on it climb one storey over each 121.00 m lap; the 3D view and the sections stand every parking level flat at its floor height, and where the core door meets the ring at each level is not drawn.

The core, as a design. Its outline is the tower plate scaled to the core area, and only that area is a computed quantity. The stairs, lifts and lobby drawn inside it, and the door into it at ground level, are an indicative layout, assumed: egress, lift traffic and fire-fighting are NOT ASSESSED, no riser or core wall is placed, and no route from the street to the core's door is drawn.

The ground floor, as a services design. Every room in its reserved strip whose width is a typical figure is an assumption: it is not sized, ventilated or access-checked against a Civil Defence or municipality requirement. The substation and the LV room are sized from DEWA §11.4.1 and §11.2.3, and neither is ventilated or access-checked either — §11.5.1 is only partly mechanizable and is NOT ASSESSED. GARBAGE ROOM: GARBAGE ROOM needs 4.00 m along the strip and 2.00 m of its 13.00 m is left, so it was not drawn rather than drawn narrow. TEL ROOM: TEL ROOM needs 2.50 m along the strip and 2.00 m of its 13.00 m is left, so it was not drawn rather than drawn narrow.
